correctness.rationale: Exact q=2 Taylor return gives two quadratic bottleneck jets, each with leading A=16π²a and shared minimum K=π²c²(16a²-c²)/(4a). At positive K their two positive-definite joint (t,epsilon) forms force constant return-drift sign; dominated bottleneck integration yields Iepsilon~2π/(sqrt(AK)*epsilon²). The relative discrete passage-time error is O(|epsilon|) since ||Dprime||=O(|epsilon|), giving rho=1/2+sgn(epsilon)*sqrt(AK)*epsilon²/(4π)+o(epsilon²). At negative K continuity forces a genuine period-two point; at c=0 an explicit two-cycle persists. Both signs of epsilon are covered; symbolic checker verifies coefficients and sampled comparisons supplement exact proof.

value.rationale: The equality min(a+Psi)=0 is exactly the meaningful excluded boundary of the recent rational-rotation scaling theorem, and nonresonant harmonic forcing can decide whether the tongue-edge path stays locked or escapes. The exact |c|=4a cutoff, nonzero signed quadratic coefficient and failure of twice differentiability distinguish three qualitatively different local regimes. This is a motivated structural limitation of first-order transversality, not a routine derivative substitution or arbitrary numeric slice.
